author: Ignatius of Antioch
ref: Ephesians 18 (ANF chapter 18; subsection 18.2 as numbered in Funk/Lightfoot not checked)
original_edition: Greek not obtained in this run (earlychristianwritings holds only the Lightfoot English for this letter)
english: For our God, Jesus Christ, was, according to the appointment of God, conceived in the womb by Mary, of the seed of David, but by the Holy Ghost.
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (ccel.org PDF anf01)
what_it_says: Ignatius says Jesus was conceived by Mary, 'of the seed of David'; the phrase grammatically describes Jesus's conception, so it is ambiguous whether it states Mary's own descent.
limits: Ambiguous as evidence that Mary herself descends from David; Greek not checked.

author: Ignatius of Antioch
ref: Ephesians ch. 20 (ANF chapter 20, 'Promise of another letter')
original_edition: Greek not obtained in this run
english: ...in Jesus Christ, who was of the seed of David according to the flesh, being both the Son of man and the Son of God...
what_it_says: Ignatius calls Jesus 'of the seed of David according to the flesh'; the statement is about Jesus and does not mention Mary.
limits: Negative for Mary: silent on Mary's descent.

author: Ignatius of Antioch
ref: Trallians ch. 9 (ANF chapter 9; subsection 9.1 not checked in Greek)
original_edition: Greek not obtained in this run
english: Stop your ears, therefore, when any one speaks to you at variance with Jesus Christ, who was descended from David, and was also of Mary; who was truly born, and ate and drank.
what_it_says: Ignatius says Jesus 'was descended from David, and was also of Mary'; it names Mary as Jesus's mother and does not say explicitly that Mary descends from David.
limits: Pairs Davidic descent with Mary but does not assign the Davidic line to Mary by blood.

author: Ignatius of Antioch
ref: Smyrnaeans ch. 1 (ANF chapter 1; subsection 1.1 not checked in Greek)
original_edition: Greek not obtained in this run
english: ...that He was truly of the seed of David according to the flesh, Romans 1:3 and the Son of God according to the will and power of God; that He was truly born of a virgin...
what_it_says: Ignatius affirms that the Lord was truly of David's seed according to the flesh, and born of a virgin; the sentence is about the Lord and not about Mary's ancestry.
limits: Negative for Mary: no statement on Mary's descent.

author: Justin Martyr
ref: Dialogue 43 (ANF chapter 43)
original_edition: Greek not obtained in this run (Otto edition not read)
english: ...so it was necessary, in accordance with the Father's will, that they should have an end in Him who was born of a virgin, of the family of Abraham and tribe of Judah, and of David; in Christ the Son of God...
what_it_says: Justin says the virgin-born Christ is 'of the family of Abraham and tribe of Judah, and of David'; the 'of David' is predicated of the virgin-born one, not explicitly of Mary.
limits: Does not explicitly say that Mary is of David; the sentence is about the virgin-born Christ.

author: Justin Martyr
ref: Dialogue 45 (ANF chapter 45)
original_edition: Greek not obtained in this run (Otto edition not read)
english: ...and submitted to become incarnate, and be born of this virgin of the family of David, in order that, by this dispensation, the serpent that sinned from the beginning...
what_it_says: Justin explicitly calls the virgin, the mother of Christ, 'of the family of David'. This is the clearest Justin passage on Mary's own Davidic descent that I read.
limits: Greek not checked; one sentence in a chapter about the law and Christ.

author: Justin Martyr
ref: Dialogue 100 (ANF chapter 100, 'In what sense Christ is [called] Jacob, and Israel, and Son of Man')
what_it_says: NEGATIVE: chapter 100 has no statement that a virgin or Mary is of David's seed; it concerns Christ as Jacob, Israel and Son of Man. The claim that Dialogue 100 says 'the virgin of the seed of David' is not supported by the text I read.
limits: Read in English (newadvent chapter 100) only; the claim is a misattributed citation as far as this text goes.

author: Justin Martyr
ref: Dialogue 120 (ANF chapter 120, 'Christians were promised to Isaac, Jacob, and Judah')
english: He says that neither to Esau nor to Reuben, nor to any other; only to those of whom the Christ should arise, according to the dispensation, through the Virgin Mary.
what_it_says: NEGATIVE for 'of David': chapter 120 names the Virgin Mary as the channel of Christ's coming but does not say she is of David.
limits: English only; the 'virgin of the seed of David' wording attributed to this chapter does not appear in the text read.

author: Irenaeus of Lyons
ref: Adversus haereses III.21.5 (ANF chapter 21, section 5)
original_edition: Latin original not legible in the OCR texts I could reach (Stieren 1853 Latin text searched; Migne PG 7 OCR is Greek-only and garbled)
english: ...He whom God promised David that He would raise up from the fruit of his belly an eternal King, is the same who was born of the Virgin, herself of the lineage of David.
what_it_says: Irenaeus says the Virgin who bore Christ was herself of David's lineage: an explicit early statement that Mary descends from David.
limits: Only the English is verified here; the Latin, the only extant original for this sentence, is not read. Argument is from the prophecy's 'fruit of the belly'.

author: Irenaeus of Lyons
ref: Adversus haereses III.21.9 (ANF chapter 21, section 9)
original_edition: Latin not read
english: For Joseph is shown to be the son of Joachim and Jechoniah, as also Matthew sets forth in his pedigree. ... But Jechoniah, and all his posterity, were disinherited from the kingdom; Jeremiah thus declaring...
what_it_says: Irenaeus states the Jeconiah objection in its earliest form I read: if Jesus were Joseph's son, Jer 22 would bar him from David's throne; he uses it to argue for the virgin birth.
limits: Irenaeus does not discuss Luke's list or Mary's line here; the objection is stated, and the answer given is the virgin birth.

author: Irenaeus of Lyons
ref: Adversus haereses III.16.2 (ANF chapter 16, section 2)
original_edition: Latin not read
english: And Matthew, too, recognising one and the same Jesus Christ, exhibiting his generation as a man from the Virgin, ... says: The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
what_it_says: Irenaeus quotes Matthew 1:1 as 'son of David, son of Abraham' and reads Matthew's genealogy as presenting Christ's generation from the Virgin; he does not say Mary is of David here.
limits: No statement on Mary's own descent in this section.

author: Tertullian
ref: De carne Christi 21 (ANF chapter XXI)
original: virga ex radice, Maria ex David? Flos ex virga, filius Mariae, qui dicitur Jesus Christus, ipse erit et fructus.
original_edition: Latin, Migne PL 2 (Tertullian), De carne Christi 21, read from the djvu OCR text (archive.org patrologiaecur02mign); OCR cleaned by me, not checked against the scan
english: ...the root of Jesse is the family of David, and the stem of the root is Mary descended from David, and the blossom of the stem is Mary's son, who is called Jesus Christ...
what_it_says: Tertullian states outright that Mary is 'descended from David' and that the 'stem of the root' (Jesse's root, David's family) is Mary.
limits: Latin is from OCR, the question mark in the Latin is rhetorical in form. Tertullian's argument is from Isaiah 11:1 typology, not from genealogy.

author: Tertullian
ref: Adversus Marcionem V.8 (ANF Book V chapter VIII)
original: Christum enim in floris figura ostendit oriturum ex virga profecta de radice Jesse, id est Virgine generis David filii Jesse
original_edition: Latin, Migne PL 2, Adversus Marcionem V.8, read from the djvu OCR text (archive.org patrologiaecur02mign); OCR cleaned by me
english: ...the blossom ... rising from the root of Jesse ... the virgin of the race of David, the son of Jesse.
what_it_says: Tertullian says Christ arose 'from the virgin of the race of David, the son of Jesse', i.e. the Virgin is of David's race.
limits: English read in the ccel text 'the virgin of the race of David, the son of Jesse'; the phrase is part of a typological exposition of Isaiah 11.

author: Anonymous (pseudepigraphal)
ref: Protevangelium of James 10.1 (ANF chapter X, section 10)
original_edition: Greek not obtained in this run (Tischendorf not read)
english: And the priest remembered the child Mary, that she was of the family of David, and undefiled before God.
what_it_says: The Protevangelium states that Mary was of the family of David; no genealogy is given and Luke is not mentioned in this passage.
limits: Apocryphal narrative; the statement is about the priesthood's choice of virgins for the Temple veil, not a genealogical argument.

work: Church History I.7 (Africanus' letter to Aristides)
author: Julius Africanus (quoted by Eusebius)
ref: Eusebius, Historia ecclesiastica I.7.9-10
original_edition: Greek not obtained (Schwartz GCS edition not read)
english: But according to law he was the son of Eli, for Jacob, being the brother of the latter, raised up seed to him.
edition: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers 2nd series vol. 1 (ccel.org PDF npnf201)
what_it_says: Africanus explains Luke's list as Joseph's legal line: Joseph was son of Eli by levirate law after Jacob (Matthew's line) raised up seed for his childless brother Eli.
limits: Africanus names Joseph and Eli, not Mary; this is the key early witness against the claim that Luke gives Mary's line.

author: Augustine of Hippo
ref: De consensu evangelistarum II.2.4 (Book II, chapter II, section 4)
original: ipsam quoque Mariam de stirpe David aliquam consanguinitatem duxisse, dubitare utique non debemus.
original_edition: Latin, Migne PL 34, read from djvu OCR (archive.org patrologiaecurs226unkngoog); OCR cleaned by me; PL column not pinned
english: ...how much more ought we to accept without any hesitation the position that Mary herself also was descended in some way, according to the laws of blood, from the lineage of David?
translator: S. D. F. Salmond (NPNF1 6, ed. M. B. Riddle)
edition: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers 1st series vol. 6 (ccel.org PDF npnf106)
what_it_says: Augustine says we ought not doubt that Mary herself was descended from David's line 'in some way' according to blood; Paul's 'seed of David' supports it.
limits: Augustine's own footnote in the Latin points to Retractations 2.16 (correction not read). Augustine hedges with 'in some way'.

author: Augustine of Hippo
ref: De consensu evangelistarum II.3.5 (and II.3.29 on Heli)
original: facile est, ut adverterant duos patres habere potuisse Joseph, unum a quo genitus, alterum a quo fuerit adoptatus
original_edition: Latin, Migne PL 34, djvu OCR (cleaned); PL column not pinned
english: ...they might easily perceive that Joseph may have had two fathers,--namely, one by whom he was begotten, and a second by whom he may have been adopted. ... Luke ... has named a father for Joseph, not in the person of the father by whom he was begotten, but in that of the father by whom he was adopted...
edition: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers 1st series vol. 6 (ccel.org PDF npnf106)
what_it_says: Augustine says Luke's Heli is the adoptive father of Joseph, or the levirate father (as Africanus), and that Matthew names the begetting father, Jacob; Luke's list is not presented as Mary's.
limits: Augustine treats Luke as naming Joseph's adoptive father; no statement that Luke traces Mary's line.

author: Augustine of Hippo (objection by Faustus)
ref: Contra Faustum XXIII.4 (Faustus's objection; NPNF section 4). Aquinas cites the same passage as 'Contra Faust. xxii'
original_edition: Latin not read
english: Moreover, the Virgin herself appears to have belonged not to the tribe of Judah ... but to the priestly tribe of Levi. ... How, then, can Mary be brought within the pale of relationship to David, when she has neither father nor husband belonging to it? Consequently, Mary's son cannot possibly be the son of David, unless you can bring the mother into some connection with Joseph...
edition: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers 1st series vol. 4 (ccel.org PDF npnf104)
what_it_says: Faustus the Manichaean argues Mary was a Levite (Joachim a priest), so she cannot be of David and her son cannot be David's son unless linked to Joseph.
limits: Objection as quoted by Augustine. The 'Levite' claim comes from apocryphal writings per Augustine.

author: Augustine of Hippo
ref: Contra Faustum XXIII.8 (NPNF section 8)
original_edition: Latin not read
english: ...those who prefer the authority of the sacred Gospel to that of heretical fiction must conclude that Mary was not unconnected with the family of David, and that she was properly called the wife of Joseph...
edition: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers 1st series vol. 4 (ccel.org PDF npnf104)
what_it_says: Augustine answers Faustus: since Matthew says Christ is of David's seed and that Joseph is in the line, Mary 'was not unconnected with the family of David'. He hedges that 'some of David's blood' may have flowed in Mary.
limits: Hedged: 'It might also be the case'; the argument rests on Matthew's text and Joseph's place in it.

author: John Chrysostom
ref: In Matthaeum Homilia II, sec. 7 (NPNF Homily II, section 7; PG 57)
original_edition: Greek not legible in the Migne PG 57 OCR I obtained (archive.org bim_early-english-books-1641-1700_1860_57; Greek garbled). Latin translation of Montfaucon in the same volume, OCR: 'Quid clarius postulas, cum audis de domo et familia David Virginem fuisse!' and 'non modo enim non licebat ex alia tribu uxorem ducere, sed neque ex alia familia, id est ex alia cognatione.'
english: ...when thou hast heard that the Virgin was of the house and lineage of David? Hence it is evident that Joseph also was of the same. Yes, for there was a law, which bade that it should not be lawful to take a wife from any other stock, but from the same tribe. ... For not only was it not allowed to take a wife out of another tribe, but not even from another lineage, that is, from another kindred.
translator: Sir George Prevost, rev. M. B. Riddle (NPNF1 10)
edition: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers 1st series vol. 10 (ccel.org PDF npnf110)
what_it_says: Chrysostom argues from Luke 1:27 that the Virgin was of David's house and lineage, and then from the law of marriage within the tribe that Joseph was also of David's lineage, so that Joseph's genealogy is Mary's too.
limits: The Greek is not verified; the Mary-of-David claim here rests on the tribal marriage law (Num 36:6-8 type reasoning). Chrysostom does not say that Luke gives Mary's line.

author: John Chrysostom
ref: In Matthaeum Homilia I, sec. 14 (NPNF Homily I, section 14)
original_edition: Greek not legible; Latin translation (Montfaucon, PG 57, OCR) reads 'modo Elisabet ex Levitica tribu, cognata sit Mari'
english: ...there being also this other hard point, how Elizabeth, who was of the Levitical tribe, was kinswoman to Mary.
translator: Sir George Prevost, rev. M. B. Riddle (NPNF1 10)
edition: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers 1st series vol. 10 (ccel.org PDF npnf110)
what_it_says: Chrysostom names as a difficulty that Elizabeth, of the Levitical tribe, was kinswoman to Mary; the 'Mary a Levite' objection is therefore already in circulation in the late fourth century.
limits: Chrysostom states the difficulty; the solution is given in Homily II.

author: Ambrose of Milan
ref: Expositio Evangelii secundum Lucam III (Lk 3:23 discussion; Latin section numbering not read)
original: Nam cum vir justus fuerit Joseph, utique ex tribu sua et ex patria sua accepit uxorem, nec potuit justus facere contra id quod lege praescriptum est.
original_edition: Latin, Migne PL 15, djvu OCR (archive.org patrologiaecur15mign); OCR errors present (for example 'liierit' = fuerit, 'Josepli' = Joseph); I corrected them in the quote; no English translation read
page: PL 15 column not pinned (OCR column marker near 1316)
what_it_says: Ambrose argues that since Joseph was a righteous man, he married within his tribe and family (Num 36:6-8 law), and that Joseph's genealogy therefore contains Mary's origin ('in Joseph origine etiam origo sit Maria'). Luke's list, in his reading, traces Joseph up to Adam.
limits: Partly OCR: text is not a verified English quotation and the column is not pinned. Ambrose does not say Luke's list is Mary's; he says Joseph's origin contains hers.

work: Against Helvidius (Perpetual Virginity of Blessed Mary)
author: Jerome
ref: Adversus Helvidium, paragraph beginning 'But if anyone feels a doubt as to why the Virgin conceived' (section number not read)
original_edition: Latin not read
english: First, that by the genealogy of Joseph, whose kinswoman Mary was, Mary's origin might also be shown.
edition: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers 2nd series vol. 6 (ccel.org PDF npnf206)
what_it_says: Jerome gives as one reason for the marriage that Joseph's genealogy also shows Mary's origin, since she was his kinswoman.
limits: Jerome does not say which evangelist's list contains Mary's line; kinship is his argument.

author: John of Damascus
ref: De fide orthodoxa IV.14 (Chapter XIV, 'Concerning our Lord's genealogy and concerning the holy Mother of God')
original_edition: Greek not obtained in this run (Migne PG 94 not read)
english: ...she, being pre-ordained ... sprang at the pre-determined time from the root of David, according to the promises that were made to him. ... But that Joseph is descended from the tribe of David is expressly demonstrated by Matthew and Luke, the most holy evangelists. But Matthew derives Joseph from David through Solomon, while Luke does so through Nathan; while over the holy Virgin's origin both pass in silence.
edition: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers 2nd series vol. 9 (ccel.org PDF npnf209)
what_it_says: Damascene says Mary sprang from David's root, while Matthew and Luke both pass over Mary's origin: Luke is read as tracing Joseph through Nathan, not Mary.
limits: Important negative for 'Luke = Mary': Damascene explicitly says Luke's list is Joseph's and is silent on Mary's origin. Greek not checked.

author: Thomas Aquinas
ref: ST III q.31 a.2 ad 1 and ad 2 (Reply to Objection 1 and Objection 2; article 3 not read)
original_edition: Latin (Leonine) not read
english: So therefore we believe that Mary was also of the family of David: because we believe the Scriptures... / It is therefore possible that Elizabeth's father married a wife of the family of David... or conversely, and with greater likelihood, that the Blessed Mary's father, who was of the family of David, married a wife of the family of Aaron.
translator: Fathers of the English Dominican Province (1947)
what_it_says: Aquinas accepts that Mary was of David's family, answers the Levite objection by a Davidic father or mother, and in ad 1 relays Augustine's Contra Faustum argument.
limits: Latin not checked. Aquinas cites the Faustus passage as 'Contra Faust. xxii', a different numbering from the NPNF Book XXIII.
